novelty_boundary: The initial candidate slate was drafted before the H31 feature prototype was implemented on arena/01a10075-gemsdoe29, based at ad130c8. After rebasing onto current main, the review includes the in-repository H29 raw-RTP/gravity worming screen. H31 is not a novel worming category: its regularized RTP vertical-integration transform and explicit drift increment remain unfit and untested on spatial holdouts. After the H34 screen (2026-10-03), H34 is reported as a negative method result, and H35-H39 are registered as the next candidate slate (H35 interaction zones, H36 MT conductance edges, H37 geothermometry, H38 worm convergence/azimuth, H39 Euler depths). Novelty claims apply only to the reviewed repositories, not all competitors. Session 3 (2026-10-03): H35 (tip-corridor stress-shadow interaction) and H40 (dense continuous persistence) were pre-registered (knowledge/19), implemented, and screened on draws 24/25; all four arms failed G1 (knowledge/21, evidence/h35_h40_screen/). The untried slate re-ranked in knowledge/20 (H41, H36, H37, H42, H38/H39 merged). Novelty claims apply only to the reviewed repositories, not all competitors. 2026-10-03 (session 4): the v4 slate (knowledge/25) adds H43-H47; novelty of H41 (qfaults attribute table for prediction) and H43 (flow routing) was re-verified by a repository-wide grep over src/, scripts/ and tests/ in this session, and H45 was checked against the frozen family-C seismicity density bands.

items.status: unimplemented; priority superseded after the H35/H40 screen by the v3 slate (knowledge/20); first in line if H41 fails its own gate
items.signature: Compare opposing-face steepness and width at a coherent terrain step; a one-sided scarp may be more fault-like than a symmetric channel bank, ridge or bench.
items.why_unmapped: Fault scarps may retain terrain expression even when USGS/INGENIOUS trace layers omit the fault.
items.difference: At GEMSDOE25 commit efc4be7bb3cfdf2def12a7fb83284d3311ac9220, the code dequantizes downface_max/upface_max as separate inputs; H30-1 uses a step × cross-profile × coherence composite and H30-3 registers cross-profile scale persistence. The raw 1-m scarp-template idea is deferred. A repository-wide search of code, tests, hypotheses and knowledge at that commit found no normalized opposing-face asymmetry ratio. H32 tests that specific derived shape ratio, not another scarp-magnitude product.

items.title: Regularized pseudogravity transform and edge-drift increment
items.status: prototype implemented; frozen screen ran and failed (feature sparsity); no confirmation; new continuous field requires a separate preregistration
items.signature: Apply a documented low-wavenumber-regularized vertical-integration pseudogravity proxy to RTP, track horizontal-gradient maxima across the fixed continuation ladder, and test lateral drift separately from persistence; include a symmetric 200-m cross-field support term.
items.why_unmapped: A buried susceptibility boundary may yield a coherent gravity-equivalent edge and scale-dependent lateral path where no surface trace is mapped in USGS/INGENIOUS; this is a structural hypothesis, not a depth/fault proof.
items.difference: The H29 experiment already ran raw-RTP and isostatic-gravity worming, joint persistence, and persistence as gate/rank/head features; all four arms failed its +0.005 proxy bar. H31 tests only a different magnetic transform (regularized vertical integration before continuation) and an explicit drift feature. It must not be presented as a first test of worming or persistence.

items.title: Acquisition-line nuisance subspace / cross-line support
items.signature: Detect magnetic edge energy aligned to repeated survey flight lines and down-rank it unless it persists across continuation scales or is corroborated by another physical field.
items.why_unmapped: A real structural edge missed by USGS/INGENIOUS should not be systematically locked to the survey-flight geometry; geometry-aware artifact control could preserve cross-line fault evidence while suppressing acquisition imprints. This is an artifact-control test, not a direct fault detector.
items.difference: H29 measured an E–W/N–S persistence audit and registered a spectral-notch experiment (H29-3); H33 would instead use verified spatial flight-path geometry as a per-location nuisance control. The concept is adjacent to prior line-artifact work and is lower-ranked/blocked until the official binary and its schema/CRS/coverage/licence are validated.
items.external_data: USGS ScienceBase DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ lists flight-path ZIPs, but binaries, schema, CRS, coverage and rights remain unvalidated. Do not download/use until verified.
items.validation: blocked until official files are obtained through permitted means and their bytes, schema, CRS, coverage and licence are independently checked

items.title: Metric-native coverage emission (preregistered method test)
items.status: screened 2026-10-03: FAIL on the catalogue-hidden primary proxy (mean paired gain -0.0212, 0/4 folds), PASS on the SGMC off-catalogue secondary (+0.0535, 4/4); not eligible for confirmation
items.signature: Residual-greedy covering of the fitted probability field with the budget chosen by the metric's own marginal rule (emit while c/f > tau = 0.2*TP/(0.2*FP+0.8*|G|)), replacing distance-rule dot thinning.
items.why_unmapped: Not a geological layer: it changes where a fixed detector's prediction mass goes, and is measured on the same holdout and the same off-catalogue class as the geological arms.
items.difference: Every prior emission in the group is a spacing rule (dot_thin, geodesic dots, wormrank ordering). H34 is the first emission chosen by the metric's marginal algebra and the first with a calibrated-budget obligation; its negative primary result is retained.
items.planning_delta_dti: measured: -0.0212 mean paired gain on the catalogue-hidden proxy; +0.0535 on the SGMC off-catalogue proxy (32 paired cells)
items.validation: frozen gate in knowledge/08_preregistered_h34_coverage_emission_2026-10-03.md; result in knowledge/09_h34_results_2026-10-03.md

items.title: Structural-interaction-zone field with dilation-tendency weighting
items.status: implemented and screened 2026-10-03: G1 FAIL. A1 structural arm mean paired gain +0.0018058 (1/4 folds positive on draw 24, worst fold -0.0103489); A2 corroboration arm +0.0045885 failed the +0.005 mean and 3/4-both-draws rules; A4 union +0.0056209 passed mean/floor/budget but only 2/4 folds positive on draw 24. No confirmation draws were fit. Evidence: evidence/h35_h40_screen/ + knowledge/21_h35_h40_results_2026-10-03.md
items.signature: Explicit interaction-zone objects: overlapping sub-parallel trace tips inside a 0.5-3 km relay window, terminations/horse-tails, and normal x transverse intersections; each weighted by dilation tendency from the regional stress field and corroborated by an independent field (scarp step+coherence, potential-field ridge, or radiometric contrast).
items.why_unmapped: Step-overs/relay ramps host 32-47% of Great Basin geothermal systems and terminations 22-25%, while range-front faults host ~1% (Faulds & Hinz 2015; Gidden & Faulds 2025). Catalogue mapping follows through-going strands and systematically misses short overlapping strands - the geometry the organizer says the hidden labels add.
items.difference: Original: no reviewed repository uses tip-corridor stress-shadow interaction fields. Result: fields were dense enough to test (relay nonzero 2.2% on the visible NW fold; 1,389 accepted corridors of 25,831 candidate pairs) and emission changed in 32/32 cells; the increment still failed every robustness reading. The sigma3 105 deg source basis is recorded in knowledge/19 section 6.
items.external_data: optional USGS slip/dilation-tendency shapefile (Siler 2022, DOI 10.5066/P9YL58W6); metadata verified, sciencebase.gov unreachable from the sandbox, so the hypothesis is written to run without it
items.validation: two-proxy admission (off-catalogue class >=3/4 folds positive; catalogue-hidden loss <=0.005) on fresh draws, preregistered before fitting

items.title: Magnetotelluric conductance structural edges and cross-fault asymmetry
items.signature: Ridge of |grad cond| with across-edge non-maximum suppression plus a discrete conductance-step (asymmetry) test and coherence with a potential-field lineament.
items.why_unmapped: MT sees through cover: a blind fault that still controls fluid flow produces a subsurface conductivity boundary with no surface scarp, so a scarp-based catalogue cannot contain it.
items.difference: The repository carries raw conductance gradients as features; no reviewed repository applies a structural edge plus step-asymmetry transform to the MT surfaces.
items.planning_delta_dti: 0 to +0.010 (low confidence; the thermal/geochemical family was inert as tested in the predecessor factorial)
items.external_data: optional Peacock & Bedrosian (2022) electrical-conductance maps, DOI 10.5066/P9TWT2LU (same sandbox limitation)

items.title: Geothermometry residual and spring-cluster geometry
items.status: specified; the naive 2 m-probe version (H29-2) failed its registered proxy gate
layers: GDR 1391 well/spring chemistry (quartz, chalcedony, Na-K-Ca temperatures)
items.signature: Kernel-smoothed residual of chemistry-derived reservoir temperature against the regional heat-flow trend, weighted by spring/well clustering and restricted to off-catalogue habitat.
items.why_unmapped: A heat-flow anomaly with no mapped fault is the classic blind-system signature: heat requires a permeable pathway, and the pathway is a fault that mapping missed.
items.difference: H29-2 used residualized 2 m air-affected probe temperature; the chemistry-derived geothermometer columns of the same hash-pinned file have not been used as a spatial field anywhere in the reviewed repositories.
items.planning_delta_dti: 0 to +0.015 (very low confidence; prior negative on the naive temperature version)

items.title: Worm convergence size and cross-field azimuth consistency
items.status: specified; not implemented; merged-downgrade with H39 in the v3 slate (filter role, not feature role)
items.signature: (a) convergence size: how many 0-m edge seeds merge into one worm at the top of the ladder (a large basin of attraction implies one deep extensive source); (b) azimuth agreement between magnetic and gravity gradient directions within 300 m.
items.why_unmapped: Blind faults keep a coherent deep potential-field edge with no surface expression; convergence plus cross-field azimuth coherence discriminates real buried structure from acquisition lineation and cultural noise better than amplitude or persistence alone.
items.difference: H29 tested persistence only (gate/rank/features) and a line-orientation audit; H31 tests pseudogravity persistence and lateral drift. Convergence statistics and directional (azimuth) agreement are new to this family.
items.planning_delta_dti: 0 to +0.008 (very low confidence; prior negatives on related persistence variants)
items.validation: off-catalogue proxy primary; azimuth agreement must be reported against the flight-line azimuth

items.title: Euler-deconvolution depth selection with two-field depth consistency
items.signature: Window-based Euler deconvolution (structural index 0-1 for contacts/thin sheets; Reid et al. 1990) producing a per-cluster depth; retain edges only where the depth is resolved and deep, magnetic and gravity depths agree within tolerance, and the edge is off-catalogue.
items.why_unmapped: Explicit depth filtering removes shallow cultural and near-surface-conductor edges that a persistence proxy only weakly separates; a deep two-field-consistent edge with no surface trace is a blind-fault candidate.
items.difference: Persistence under upward continuation is an implicit depth proxy; no reviewed repository computes Euler depths or a cross-field depth-agreement test.
items.planning_delta_dti: 0 to +0.008 (very low confidence; Euler is sensitive to structural index and window size)
items.validation: report the SI/window sensitivity table alongside the screen

items.title: Dense continuous multiscale upward-continuation persistence surfaces
items.status: implemented and screened 2026-10-03: G1 FAIL. A3 mean paired gain +0.0004827 (2/4 folds positive on both draws) - inert increment, not disproven science; the E-W persistence caveat from the H29 diagnostic travels with the verdict. Cache work/h40_dense_persistence.npy sha256 444cc851...; evidence: evidence/h35_h40_screen/ and knowledge/21_h35_h40_results_2026-10-03.md
items.signature: Per-pixel min/mean edge magnitude and mean deep-scale magnitude over a frozen continuation ladder (0,100,200,400,800,1200 m) computed as dense smoothed surfaces with nearest-valid padding, not sparse peak sets; depth-proportionality prior for source-bounded edges.
items.why_unmapped: A blind or buried source boundary retains scale-invariant edge amplitude where surface-expression detectors and the supplied catalogue have nothing; dense surfaces avoid the H31 sparsity failure.
items.difference: H29 used sparse bounded persistence of worm-like tracks; H31 used seed-tracked persistence columns (0.001-0.084% nonzero). H40 is the dense continuous replacement, built from the same frozen Hornby/Boschetti/Horowitz 1999 motivation (doi:10.1111/j.1365-2478.1999.ggg031.x) but as always-defined fields. It failed by being flat, not by being empty (0/32 identical-emission cells).

The two frozen controls reproduced the stored H34 cells bit-for-bit (max |delta| = 0.0), so the comparison is valid and the earlier +0.0073/+0.0077 screen/confirmation means were draw-specific. Verdict NO PROMOTION, no candidate built, no slot; the line is closed for promotion (knowledge/28_h41a4_results_2026-10-03.md, evidence/h41a4_h34protocol/).

items.title: Measured-period acquisition-line spectral audit, then a one-shot notch
items.status: proposed in the v3 slate (refines the registered H29-3 idea); not implemented; official flight-path binary (doi:10.5066/P93LGLVQ) remains unfetchable in-sandbox, so the assumed-spacing variant stays blocked
items.signature: Estimate the dominant cross-line wavenumber per flight-line block from azimuthally banded power spectra; notch only if the peak exceeds the local continuum by a frozen margin; recompute A-ridges once.

items.difference: H29-3 registered a notch with ASSUMED spacing (200/400 m); nothing in the family measures the period from the data. The measured-period audit is new and self-verifying.
